dedupe_keys.name: commercial buildings energy consumption survey cbecs

description: CBECS is the U.S. national sample survey of commercial buildings, collecting their energy-related characteristics and their energy consumption and expenditures. It is run by the U.S. Energy Information Administration; commercial buildings are those with at least half their floor space used for purposes that are not residential, industrial or agricultural, so the survey also covers schools, hospitals, prisons and places of worship as well as offices, shops, restaurants and warehouses. According to the 2018 survey's final results, the estimated 5.9 million U.S. commercial buildings used 6.8 quadrillion Btu of energy and spent 141 billion dollars on it, mainly electricity and natural gas, with space heating close to one third of end use; in 2024 EIA published exploratory post-pandemic surveys of office and education buildings to prepare the next cycle. Access: data tables, reports and public-use microdata from EIA; Catalyst Cooperative archives the raw inputs for 1992 to 2018 on Zenodo. Licence: U.S. government data in the public domain; free. Caveats: a sample survey with years between cycles. Simulation uses are commercial and public building stock energy models, including hospitals and schools, and benchmarks for calibration. Related records: the Residential Energy Consumption Survey and EnergyPlus.
